author: Codex blind first-pass assessor

source_artifacts.claim: The room source defines Pac and Isp spawns, the two character-specific pads, route gates, stable/lower platforms, exits, and the fixed Cana boomerang.
A boomerang hit gives Isp DIZZY or Pac SHOVE; Pac receives horizontal velocity in projectile direction.
Cana boomerang windup/release is automatic after cooldown; no player attack control is required.
Projectile motion and player collisions apply the temporary effect; the projectile returns after reaching its endpoint.
Isp SAFE LANDING is a hold and Pac OPEN ISP is a latch; active pad effects stabilize the deck/open gates.
Earlier level_41 introduces Cana boomerang and character-specific gates/pads; campaign exposure is not proof of mastery.

prior_knowledge.concept: Cana boomerang with Isp DIZZY/Pac SHOVE role cue was introduced at campaign position 11. Level_36 reuses the same hit roles but applies Pac shove as traversal help and pairs it with an Isp-held safe landing and Pac latch.

evidence.claim: Position 11 authors the boomerang, Isp/Pac roles, and a route pad; authored exposure does not establish mastery.
The earlier canvas visibly names ISP DIZZY / PAC SHOVE.

prior_knowledge.concept: Character-specific automatic pads, latches, and opening routes were introduced earlier, including level_08 and level_12; here their familiar form is combined with an automatically aimed projectile.

evidence.claim: Position 7 uses character-specific steady and rescue pads to stabilize a route and open a gate.
The earlier capture visibly labels the role-specific pads and crate/plate.

mechanics.fact: Cana automatically throws a boomerang on a fixed path after cooldown and windup. On hit, Isp gets DIZZY; Pac gets SHOVE with horizontal velocity in the projectile travel direction. Players do not aim or press an attack key.

evidence.claim: The level defines a fixed-target Cana boomerang with 0.35-second windup and 1.4-second cooldown.
After cooldown the attacker enters windup, then releases the projectile automatically.
A hit applies Isp dizzy or Pac shove; shove velocity follows projectile direction.

mechanics.fact: Isp must occupy SAFE LANDING (a hold) to stabilize the far deck and open Pac’s membrane. Pac is hit by the right-going Cana throw, uses the extra push to cross to the far deck, then occupies OPEN ISP, a latch that opens the Isp gate and Pac membrane and stabilizes the deck after Pac leaves.

evidence.claim: The pads, gates, and unstable deck are authored with the stated effects.
Hold effects follow occupancy; latches persist; active effects open barriers and stabilize platforms.
The correct stable-ID route moves Isp onto the upper safe landing while Pac advances into Cana’s projectile path.
Pac has crossed onto the far deck after the shove, while Isp remains in the upper route.
The native stable level_36 route completes with both exits and zero deaths.

mechanics.fact: The unstable far deck collapses after 2.5 seconds of occupancy unless stabilized and respawns after 2 seconds. SAFE LANDING and OPEN ISP both stabilize it; the lower recovery floor and no configured hazards make failed jumps recoverable in principle.

evidence.claim: The level defines the unstable deck and continuous recovery floor.
Both pads stabilize the deck; no hazards are authored.
Unstable platform collapse/respawn follows configured occupancy and reset intervals.

mechanics.fact: Once Pac latches OPEN ISP, Isp crosses the upper route and exits; Pac traverses the lower route to the matching exit. Both exits are required.

evidence.claim: The Pac membrane and Isp gate separate routes and each hero has a matching exit.
The attempt records complete status with both matching exits true and zero deaths.

legal_routes.name: Ordinary-input safe-landing / automatic shove / OPEN ISP route

steps.goal: Hold the safe landing and stabilize the far deck.
steps.action: Move along the upper route onto SAFE LANDING and remain there.
steps.expected_feedback: The far deck stays stable and the Pac membrane opens while Isp occupies the hold; the route trace shows Isp reaching the pad area, but does not record pad-state feedback.

evidence.claim: SAFE LANDING is Isp-only hold, stabilizing the far deck and opening Pac membrane.
Isp moves right to the upper pad while Pac advances below.

steps.goal: Use Cana’s automatic right-going shove to cross to the far deck.
steps.action: Move/jump right through Cana’s fixed projectile lane, then continue over the gap to the far deck.
steps.expected_feedback: A hit applies temporary Pac SHOVE; the trace shows Pac advancing over the gap and reaching the far deck without death.
steps.observed_feedback: The scripted input route advances Pac from x250 toward x590 and reaches the far deck; no human response was observed.

evidence.claim: Pac boomerang hits apply a temporary right/left horizontal push based on projectile direction.
Pac moves from the launch area onto the far deck without death during the ordinary-input trace.

steps.goal: Latch OPEN ISP and free Isp.
steps.action: Occupy OPEN ISP on the far deck; leave only after the latch is active.
steps.expected_feedback: The latch opens Isp’s gate and Pac membrane and stabilizes the deck; effects persist after Pac leaves.

evidence.claim: OPEN ISP is Pac-only latch that opens both gates and stabilizes the deck.
Pac reaches the far deck before Isp crosses the gate.

steps.action: Isp crosses the upper route to ISP EXIT; Pac follows the lower route to PAC EXIT.
steps.expected_feedback: Both matching exits together finish the level.
steps.observed_feedback: The stable level_36 attempt finishes both exits with zero deaths in 5.9083 seconds.

evidence.claim: The two matching exits are authored.
The route completes both exits with zero deaths.
Current stable-ID ordinary-input trace completes both exits with zero deaths; scripted feasibility does not establish human discovery.

isp: Holds SAFE LANDING so Pac’s route membrane opens and the far deck is stabilized; after Pac latches OPEN ISP, crosses upper route to the Isp exit.
pac: Receives Cana’s right-going shove to cross the gap, latches OPEN ISP to open Isp’s gate and stabilize the deck, then reaches Pac’s lower exit.

common_mistakes.mistake: Isp leaves SAFE LANDING before Pac latches OPEN ISP.
common_mistakes.consequence: The hold effects end; the far deck can resume its 2.5-second collapse timer and Pac’s membrane closes.
common_mistakes.recovery: Isp can return to the upper pad; if the deck has collapsed it respawns after two seconds. This is mechanics-derived, not exercised in the no-death trace.

evidence.claim: SAFE LANDING is an occupancy-based hold and stabilizes the deck.
Unstabilized occupied deck collapses and respawns after its reset interval.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac misses the shove-assisted jump and falls to the lower return floor.
common_mistakes.consequence: Pac loses route progress but no room hazard is configured; the bottom floor remains available.
common_mistakes.recovery: Retry the traversal after returning to the launch/step area; exact path and time were not exercised. Source hint mentions a lower return fold but is not used to rate base clarity.

evidence.claim: A continuous recovery floor is authored beneath the route and the far deck is unstable.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac leaves OPEN ISP before activating it.
common_mistakes.consequence: Isp’s gate remains closed and the deck may become unstable after Pac leaves.
common_mistakes.recovery: Return Pac to the far-deck latch; source and successful route support that it can be activated there, but this mistake was not attempted.

evidence.claim: OPEN ISP latches the gate and stabilizes the deck when Pac occupies it.

reasoning.rationale: The sequence requires identifying Isp’s hold as the support for Pac, then using the incoming automatic shove to cross and latching OPEN ISP to release Isp. The authored labels cue roles but not the complete dependency chain; the ordinary trace confirms feasibility.

evidence.claim: The two pads have distinct gates/stabilization effects and require a handoff.
The canvas visibly labels the safe landing and Pac OPEN ISP pad but does not draw their causal links.
A current stable-ID trace completes the route, proving feasibility only.

cooperation.rationale: Isp must hold the upper route while Pac uses the shove and latches the far pad; Pac’s latch then frees Isp. Both roles are necessary, with one clear handoff.

evidence.claim: Isp hold and Pac latch have complementary route effects.
Pac reaches the far deck while Isp remains on the upper route.

execution.rationale: Pac must use a moving shove during a jump across a gap and land on the far deck, while Isp traverses a long upper route. The 5.9-second scripted clear has zero deaths, but is not a human error-rate measure.

evidence.claim: The level requires a jump across the gap to the far deck.
Pac crosses from the launch area to the far deck in the scripted trace.
The route completes with zero deaths.

timing.rationale: Cana’s projectile has a repeatable automatic cooldown/windup and the shove must coincide with Pac’s traversal, but the projectile recurs and there is no authored narrow window. The trace completes without a timing failure.

evidence.claim: The throw uses a repeatable 1.4-second cooldown and 0.35-second windup.
The attack repeats automatically after cooldown/windup.
A scripted route succeeds without death; this does not establish novice timing.

hazards.rationale: There are no authored hazards on the mandatory route; a continuous lower floor and recovery floor underlie the gap. Falling out of world bounds is fatal generally, but is not a required exposure here.

evidence.claim: The lower recovery floor lies under the route.
No hazard objects are defined and exits are above the continuous route.

novelty.rationale: The boomerang’s Isp-dizzy/Pac-shove roles were introduced earlier at level_41, and role-specific pads/latches are familiar from earlier rooms. The new teaching combination uses the automatic shove as traversal help while another hero holds a safe landing, then transfers to a latch.

evidence.claim: Position 11 introduces Cana’s boomerang and role-specific pad/gate use.
Current room combines the reused boomerang with new safe-landing and OPEN ISP pad dependencies.

recovery_cost.rationale: A failed crossing can fall to a continuous lower return floor; the far deck also respawns after two seconds if it collapses. The route itself has no failure, so recovery is inferred from authored geometry/mechanics rather than a tested mistake.

evidence.claim: A continuous recovery floor and an unstable deck with a two-second reset are authored.
Unstable deck respawns after its configured interval.

solution_clarity.rationale: The subtitle says free Isp, and the canvas labels BOOMERANG roles, SAFE LANDING, and OPEN ISP. Players still must discover that the periodic Cana throw supplies Pac’s horizontal boost and that Pac’s latch opens Isp’s gate; exact relation is not shown.

evidence.claim: The visible subtitle says to return the favor and free Isp.
Visible role cue and pad labels expose candidate roles but not the causal route.

control_friction.rationale: The two heroes use separate movement keys; Cana’s boomerang is automatic rather than a player-triggered ability, and the stable-ID script completes the room using ordinary movement/jump input. This does not measure human comfort.

evidence.claim: Isp and Pac have distinct keyboard mappings.
The ordinary-input scripted route completes with both exits and zero deaths.

confidence_reason: Source, captured labels, and a correctly attributed stable level_36 ordinary-input trace establish the mechanics and a feasible zero-death route. No human action or mistake was observed, so discovery, actual precision burden, and recovery remain expert estimates.

confirmed: The visible subtitle’s “free Isp” objective matches the source route: Isp holds SAFE LANDING while Pac uses the shove and latches OPEN ISP.
The earlier level_41 role cue correctly suggested Pac receives SHOVE and Isp DIZZY; the current source confirms that transfer.
The idle images did not show actions; the first pass correctly left observed feedback null.
missed_mechanics: Cana’s boomerang is an automatic fixed-target hazard, not a player-aimed or player-triggered action; a hit gives Pac right-going shove and Isp dizzy.
Isp SAFE LANDING is a hold that stabilizes the far deck and opens Pac’s membrane; Pac OPEN ISP is a latch that opens the Isp gate and stabilizes the deck.
A successful ordinary route takes Pac across to OPEN ISP while Isp holds, then sends both along separate matching exits.
The deck collapses after 2.5 seconds of occupancy unless stabilized and returns after two seconds; the room has no authored hazards.
incorrect_inferences: No specific first-pass fact was proven false; its aim/target questions were explicitly unknown. The idea that players must aim or trigger the boomerang is not retained as a fact: source shows it is automatic.
changed_judgments: Reasoning rises from 2 to 3 because the source reveals a two-stage causal dependency (Isp hold, Pac shove and latch) beyond the broad return-favor cue.
Cooperation remains 3; source confirms the separating roles and release handoff are mandatory.

Execution rises from 2 to 3 because the mandatory route includes a shove-assisted gap crossing plus long separate upper/lower traversals; the current script clears without deaths but does not estimate human errors.

Timing changes from null to 1: Cana’s throw runs automatically on a repeating cooldown/windup, and Pac must cross during the shove, but the effect is repeatable and there is no narrow one-shot window.
Hazards change from null to 0 because the level has no authored hazard objects and the lower return floor provides refuge; lethal out-of-world falls are not required exposure.
Novelty remains 2: the boomerang roles were introduced at level_41 and pad/latch roles earlier, while using shove as a traversal aid plus safe-landing support is a new combination.
Recovery changes from null to 1 because the lower floor and two-second deck respawn support local retry; no failed attempt tested that route.
Solution clarity remains 2: visible labels and subtitle identify candidate roles, while automatic shove-to-crossing and pad-to-gate links still need discovery.
Control friction changes from null to 0 because movement mappings are separate, the shove is automatic, and a scripted ordinary-input route succeeds; no human comfort was measured.
unresolved: No human first-encounter route or recovery was observed; scripted feasibility does not establish difficulty or discovery.
The no-death trace does not test a missed jump or early release of SAFE LANDING/OPEN ISP.
The exact movement margins for landing on OPEN ISP and the far deck are not measured from human play.

single_operator_note: A single operator must alternate between Isp W/A/D and Pac arrow keys while monitoring the automatic boomerang and keeping Isp on SAFE LANDING until Pac reaches OPEN ISP. The route evidence does not measure one-operator comfort.
